results.note: HAZ cargo cannot go on a SOC line
results.response: No, hazardous cargo cannot be quoted on a SOC line: SOC lines only accept general cargo and are not approved for dangerous goods. Flammable liquids (IMO class 3) must be quoted on a price line flagged HAZ, with Northwind equipment; a HAZ surcharge is added to the base rate and a dangerous goods declaration is required before booking. If the customer insists on shipping the hazardous cargo in its own container, that is a special rate: send the request to the Pricing desk.

results.note: SOC meaning and why it is cheaper
results.response: The SOC flag marks a price line for shipper-owned containers: it applies when the customer ships in its own container instead of Northwind equipment (flag added in TideRate 3.2). SOC rates are lower because Northwind does not provide, reposition or maintain the container; on Le Havre to Shanghai the SOC line is usually 150 to 250 USD below the standard 40HC rate. SOC lines only accept general cargo.

QuotePort returns no offer because lithium batteries are not in the commodity list. Send the commodity request form to the commodity data team (commodity-data@northwind.example) with the commodity name, the HS code and the IMO class; lead time is two business days. Open the quote in QuotePort and check that its status is ACCEPTED or PENDING, click Convert to booking, select a voyage, then confirm the equipment and quantity. The booking total is the quoted all-in price per container multiplied by the number of containers. A quote is valid for 14 days from its creation date; the validity date is printed on the quote. After that it cannot be converted: create a new quote, which uses the current ACTIVE price line, so the price may change.

results.note: Answer found in a video transcript
results.response: From the dynamic pricing demo video: dynamic prices are recalculated every six hours from vessel utilisation and recent bookings. They never go below the floor price, which is the higher of two values: the cost of the voyage leg plus the minimum margin of 8 percent, or 90 percent of the published ACTIVE rate. Dynamic pricing is in beta on the North Europe to Asia trade only (TideRate 3.3).

BAF (bunker adjustment factor) covers fuel price changes; LSS (low sulphur surcharge) covers the extra cost of low-sulphur fuel required by emission rules. Both are charged per container on top of the base rate. The customer always sees an all-in price in QuotePort, so the line's surcharges are included in the quoted price. On price lists published all-in, the rates already contain every surcharge and nothing is added on top.
